notes: Dev-split TBox revision. The class rule is the definition of a Type II supernova (core collapse of a massive star, Wikipedia's lead), with no real exception: even electron-capture supernovae come from stars of 8 to 10 solar masses. The revision swaps the progenitor for a brown dwarf, a counterfactual that crosses a physical boundary (a brown dwarf never ignites hydrogen). The three derived questions name real but little-known Type II supernovae (SN 1968D, SN 1961I, SN 1964F: from before progenitor searches, so no stored per-member progenitor), with the membership stated in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application (what to look for in archival images). Original answers name the accepted alternative ("a massive star (such as a red supergiant)"), since a red supergiant is the usual expert answer for a Type II-P progenitor; the judge reads either as the original. The near unrelated question (Type Ia: a white dwarf) differs from the new answer and catches an edit that spreads to supernovae in general.
